memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Then the LORD said to Moses, 'Why are you crying out to me? Tell the Israelites
to move on. Raise your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea to divide
the water so that the Israelites can go through the sea on dry ground.'"
- Ex 14:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is one of the surprises of the chapter. Moses has just told the people to
stand still, and God says, "Why are you crying out to me? Tell them to move on."

There is a time to be still and a time to walk. Both are obedience. The
difference is whether God has spoken.

Before God gave instructions, stillness was right. Once He gave instructions,
continued crying out would have been delay dressed up as devotion. Prayer is not
a substitute for obedience. Sometimes the most spiritual thing is to stop
praying about it and do what God has already said.

Notice what God asks of Moses: raise your staff. That staff had no power in
itself. It was a shepherd's stick. But it was the visible act of obedience God
attached His power to.

Notice also the order. God did not part the sea and then say move. He said move,
and the parting came as they obeyed. Later, at the Jordan, the priests had to
step into the water before it stopped flowing (Josh 3:13).

Faith often takes the first step before it sees the path.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there something you keep praying about that God has already told you to
   do?
2. What first step are you waiting to take until the way is fully clear?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, show me when to be still and when to move. Give me courage to take the
step before I can see the whole path. Amen.
